rule.one_paragraph: A market earns a card when it passes one of three gates, and keeps it while our own reel keeps talking about it. SCHEDULED: it prices a release or meeting that sits on the ECONOMIC tape (CPI, core CPI, PCE, payrolls, GDP, the Fed, ECB, BoJ; the midterms count as a dated event) — mapped by Polymarket series so it rolls to the next print by itself. SERVED: its title names an instrument we serve (Bitcoin, Ethereum, gold, WTI, the S&P, the 10- and 30-year, 'largest company', a megacap by name) or a sector fund's theme (AI capex / semis for SMH, oil for XLE and USO, gold for GLD, data centres for the AI names) — shown on that instrument's page as well as on the master tab. REEL: a geopolitical or policy theme whose headline count in our 7-day reel is at least 100. Everything else stays out of the cards and lives in a one-line 'what Polymarket is trading' footer.
rule.floor: A topic keeps its card while its 7-day reel count is ≥ 100; between 20 and 99 it moves to a quieter WATCHING row; below 20 it is proposed for retirement at the next review — never dropped silently. Alan's standing rule holds: enduring topics (China–Taiwan, Iran, the carry trade…) roll forward and must not disappear when one question ends.
rule.measurement: one nightly SQL over public.news titles (one regular expression per topic, the same ones used for the scan in raw/), written to a small table prediction_topic_health (topic, reel_7d, volume_24h, gate, status) and printed on each card — so a topic's place is a number, not an opinion. That table does not exist yet; it would be an additive migration (pre-approved class) when built.
